properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Saturday July 25 to 400 PM Sunday July 26

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Hot and sunny weather will allow ozone to
reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups level on Saturday and
Sunday.  For Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts, and
advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Sunday, July 26, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone pollution
through state policies. For more information about health impacts
and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

Lower Columbia Basin of Oregon, 691 Lower Columbia Basin of
Washington, 697 Central Blue Mountains and 704 Northern
Deschutes National Forest.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread

are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.areaDesc: Lincoln, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 25 at 3:49PM MDT until July 25 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 349 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain over the South Fork Burn Scar. Up
to 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to
0.1 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Upper Canyon, Brady
Canyon, and Perk Canyon as well as the Cedar Creek, Eagle Creek and
Rio Ruidoso drainages. Impacts will include but are not limited to
all nearby reservoirs, bridges, culverts and roadways. Impacts to
areas along the Rio Ruidoso may extend downstream of Ruidoso Downs.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the South Fork Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges. A rain gauge on the South Fork
burn scar measured 1.21 inches in 30 minutes.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
South Fork Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ruidoso, Ruidoso Downs, Alto, Glencoe and Hollywood.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the South Fork Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 25 at 2:30PM MST until July 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 106 to
113 degrees. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Dripping Springs, Globe/Miami, San Carlos, and Tonto Basin.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 25 at 3:18PM MDT until July 25 at 5:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 318 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 0.25 and 0.5 inches of rain have
fallen between Zuni Pueblo and Black Rock. Additional rainfall
amounts up to 0.25 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Zuni Pueblo and Black Rock.

Areas along Old Gallup Road, Sandy Springs Road, and Lakeside Drive
in northeast Zuni Pueblo will be most vulnerable to potential flash
flooding impacts.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

properties.description:

currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Live Oak, TX; McMullen, TX
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 25 at 2:26PM CDT until July 26 at 2:36PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Frio River At Tilden affecting McMullen and Live Oak Counties.

For the Frio River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this evening and continue falling to 7.0 feet early Thursday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 22.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 22.8
feet on 02/05/1992.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.areaDesc: Dimmit, TX
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 25 at 2:20PM CDT until July 26 at 11:36AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Asherton affecting Dimmit County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until late tomorrow morning.

* IMPACTS...At 22.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding reaches into low
lying areas of the flood plain. Livestock and equipment should be
moved from vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 22.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 1:30 PM CDT Saturday was 24.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
late this evening and continue falling to 7.3 feet early
Thursday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
21.2 feet on 12/23/1991.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning by 830 AM CDT.

* WHERE...Barton, Ellsworth, Lincoln, McPherson, Rice, Russell, and
Saline Counties.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued July 25 at 11:37AM PDT until July 26 at 12:00AM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected on southward
facing beaches.

* WHERE...The Lost Coast and the Mendocino Coast.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

* WHEN...From 8 AM EDT this morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...The cold water temperatures can quickly cause
hypothermia to anyone immersed in the waters. Anyone on boats

properties.instruction:

number of boats and paddlecraft are expected to be out on the
water and when warm air temperatures may cause people to
underestimate the danger of the cold water. Paddle smart from the
start. Always wear your life jacket. Be aware of wind conditions,
tides, and localized currents.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 25 at 10:19AM PDT until July 25 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
...HOT DRY WINDY CONDITIONS IN NW NEVADA TODAY...

.Relative humidity in the single digits combined with afternoon
westerly wind gusts of 30-33 mphs will create hazardous fire
weather conditions.

The National Weather Service in Elko has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect until 8 PM PDT this evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zone 437.

* WIND...30-33 mph gusts

* HUMIDITY...4-10%

* THUNDERSTORMS...0% chance

* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A red flag warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 25 at 12:19PM CDT until July 25 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Heat Advisory, heat index values up to
107. For the second Heat Advisory, heat index values up to 108
expected.

* WHERE...Portions of north central and northeast Texas.

* WHEN...For today's Heat Advisory, until 8 PM CDT this evening.
For Sunday's Heat Advisory, from noon to 8 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity will increase the
risk for heat-related illnesses to occur, particularly for
those working or participating in outdoor activities.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out
of the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young
children and pets should never be left unattended in vehicles
under any circumstances.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when
possible. To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational
Safety and Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent
rest breaks in shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone
overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded location.
Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Modoc County Except for the Surprise Valley; Klamath Basin and the Fremont-Winema National Forest
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 25 at 9:46AM PDT until July 26 at 7:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
...Critical fire weather conditions continue through the
weekend...

.Hot, dry and windy conditions will peak this afternoon east of
the Cascades. Humidities trend slightly higher today and will
continue that slight trend higher into Sunday.

...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 1 PM TO 7 PM PDT SUNDAY
FOR STRONG GUSTY WIND AND LOW RH FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONES 285 AND
624...

* AFFECTED AREA...In Oregon, Fire weather zone 624 covering the
Klamath Basin and Fremont-Winema National Forest. In California,
fire weather zone 285 covering Modoc County except for Surprise
Valley. The areas of concern shrink to southern portions of fwz
624 Sunday.

* WINDS...Southwest to west 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 40 mph
Saturday and 35 mph Sunday.

* MINIMUM HUMIDITY...8 to 15 percent. Humidities rise slightly
on Sunday.

* DURATION...3 to 6 hours Saturday and Sunday afternoon and
evening.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Follow all fire restrictions. You can find your county's
emergency sign up form as well as links to fire restrictions at
weather.gov/medford/wildfire. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Be sure you're signed up for your county's emergency alert
system. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan and make
sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for
more information.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions
that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

NWSheadline: RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 PM PDT THIS EVENING FOR STRONG GUSTY WIND AND LOW RH FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONES 285 AND 624

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Surprise Valley California; Eastern Lassen County; Northern Washoe County
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 25 at 9:29AM PDT until July 26 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Reno has issued a Red Flag
Warning for gusty winds and low humidity, which is in effect from
1 PM to 9 PM PDT Sunday. The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in
effect.

* CHANGES...Increased wind speeds.

* Affected Area...Fire Weather Zone 270 Surprise Valley
California, Fire Weather Zone 278 Eastern Lassen County, Fire
Weather Zone 458 Northern Washoe County.

* Winds...Southwest 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 30 to 40 mph.

* Humidity...Afternoon minimums 5 to 11 percent through Sunday.
Overnight recoveries 25 to 45 percent each night through Monday
morning.

* Duration...3 to 7 hours Saturday afternoon. 3 to 6 hours
Sunday afternoon.

* Impacts...The combination of gusty winds and low humidity can
cause fire to rapidly grow in size and intensity before first
responders can contain them.
properties.instruction:
Avoid outdoor activities that can cause a spark near dry
vegetation, such as yard work, target shooting, or campfires.
Follow local fire restrictions. Check weather.gov/reno for
updates and livingwithfire.info for preparedness tips.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 25 at 11:24AM CDT until July 26 at 5:54PM CDT by NWS Topeka KS
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Kansas...

Salt Creek near Ada affecting Ottawa County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Salt Creek near Ada.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Minor low land flooding along the Salt
Creek. At 20.0 feet, 50th Road just south of the bridge over the
Salt Creek floods. At 20.2 feet, Deck of 50th Road bridge over the
Salt Creek floods. At 21.0 feet, Flood waters are over one half
mile wide over cultivated farm land 3 miles east southeast of the
town of Ada.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 19.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.4 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late tonight.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

This product along with additional weather and stream information is
available at www.weather.gov/top/.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures in the
mid to upper 100s expected. Low temperatures around 80 degrees
will provide little relief from the heat. HeatRisk will be in the
purple (extreme) range to the red (major) range through the
weekend.

* WHERE...Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell.

* WHEN...Until midnight MDT Monday Night.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Gulf
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued July 25 at 11:16AM EDT until July 26 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Gulf County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Westerly swell over the Gulf waters this
morning will combine with westerly breezes and the afternoon
seabreeze to bring development of a high risk for rip currents
this afternoon and evening, mainly over west-facing beaches of
Gulf and Bay Counties.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 25 at 9:14AM MDT until July 27 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 110 expected.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest and west central Kansas and southwest
Nebraska.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM CDT /9 PM MDT/ Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Livestock may be stressed as well due to
multiple days of triple digit heat.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The hottest day of this period is currently
forecast to be Sunday where air temperatures are forecast to exceed
105 degrees. For Saturday, there is some question about how high
heat indices may get as drier air may get pulled down from aloft.
This signal weakens some for Sunday, so Sunday may be the most
impactful day for heat related impacts. Minimal overnight recovery
is also forecast as temperatures may not fall below 70-75 degrees.
properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 25 at 9:20AM EDT until July 26 at 4:10PM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Georgia...

Big Creek near Alpharetta affecting Fulton and Forsyth Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Creek near Alpharetta.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor flooding expands along the creek from
near Cumming to Alpharetta and Roswell. Backyards of homes off
Seale Drive and Gunter Court and portions of the Golf of Georgia
begin to flood. The Big Creek Greenway experiences significant
flooding up to 3 feet deep...which results in closure of most of
the paths. This especially occurs upstream and downstream from the
gage on Kimball Bridge Road and Rock Mill Park. A large portion of
the YMCA Campground off Preston Ridge Road will be under a foot of
water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 8.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:45 AM EDT Saturday was 9.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 1.9 feet Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at weather.gov/atlanta.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 25 at 8:20AM EDT until July 25 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of eastern North Carolina, including the
following counties, Dare and Hyde.

* WHEN...Until 800 PM EDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 818 AM EDT, emergency management reported water still on
roadways of portions of NC12 from heavy rain in the advisory
area due to multiple days of thunderstorms. Overflowing poor
drainage areas will cause minor flooding in the advisory
area. Between 1 and 5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected
over the area through today. This additional rain will result
in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Frisco, Southern Shores, Nags Head, Rodanthe, Waves, Salvo,
Buxton, Manteo, Colington, Roanoke Island Festival Park,
Hatteras Island Fishing Pier, Cape Hatteras Lighthouse and
Hatteras Ferry Terminal.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 25 at 6:02AM MDT until July 25 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 1 PM TO 9 PM MDT TODAY FOR
SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS FOR IDAHO FIRE WEATHER ZONES 410, 413, AND
427...

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 410 Upper Snake River
Valley/Idaho Falls BLM, Fire Weather Zone 413 Caribou
Range/Caribou NF and Fire Weather Zone 427 Goose Creek and
Raft River Valley/Southern Sawtooth NF/Twin Falls BLM south of
the Snake River.

* IMPACTS...Scattered thunderstorms can produce frequent
lightning that may in turn produce wildfire starts in
receptive fuels.

* THUNDERSTORMS...A mix of wet and dry storms.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusts over 35 mph with peak gusts nearing 45-
55 mph.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly based on these criteria
for Southeastern Idaho:

- Relative humidity at or below 15 percent and wind gusts of at
least 25 mph in the mountains, or 30 mph in the Snake Plain.

- Thunderstorm coverage of 25 percent, without specific rainfall
criteria.

- Other high impact events deemed critical by the National
Weather Service and area fire management agencies.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 25 at 2:29AM MST until July 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with temperatures of 100 to 105
expected with Major HeatRisk.

* WHERE...Eastern Cochise County below 5000 feet, Upper San Pedro
River Valley, and Upper Santa Cruz River Valley/Altar Valley.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 25 at 12:47AM MST until July 25 at 9:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions, with temperatures up to 113
expected.

* WHERE...Yavapai County Valleys and Basins.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 9 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Grand Canyon Country
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 25 at 12:47AM MST until July 26 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected below 4000 feet, with
daytime temperatures around 105 degrees at Havasupai Gardens, and
112 to 114 degrees at Phantom Ranch.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of the Grand Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
This warning is reserved for only the hottest days of the year and is
issued when temperatures are expected to rise to dangerous levels.

Day hikers on Bright Angel Trail should descend no farther than 1 1/2
miles from the upper trailhead. Between the hours of 10 AM and 4 PM,
hikers should be out of the canyon or at Havasupai Gardens or Bright
Angel campgrounds, physical activity is discouraged. All hikers
should have adequate gear, including a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen,
salty snacks, sufficient water, and electrolyte mix. Doubling your
calorie intake helps maintain your energy.

Hike smart.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Little Susitna River from the Parks Highway downstream.

* WHEN...Until 1100 PM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1054 PM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the advisory area. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
- The crest is expected to occur near the Parks Highway
overnight tonight in minor flood stage and the begin to
recede. Areas farther downstream toward the Susitna Landing
Public Use area will likely not see the  river crest until
Saturday night or Sunday morning.
- For Little Susitna at Houston:
At 9:50pm the stage was 11.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 11.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 11.3 feet is expected around 4:00am
Saturday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 24 at 4:19PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the following agencies:

Idaho Department of Environmental Quality in Lewiston
Nez Perce Tribe

...AIR QUALITY ADVISORY FROM THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY FOR Clearwater, Idaho, Latah, Lewis, and Nez Perce
Counties...

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke. Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...Clearwater, Idaho, Latah, Lewis, and Nez Perce Counties...

* WHEN...Until noon July 27th.

* IMPACTS...Members of sensitive groups may experience health
effects. The general public is less likely to be affected.
properties.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

THIS STATEMENT IS ISSUED BY THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY, AIR QUALITY GROUP FOR MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT DEQ's
Lewiston Regional Office at (208) 799-4370

properties.areaDesc: Kivalina and Red Dog Dock; Baldwin Peninsula; Northern Seward Peninsula; Shishmaref
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 24 at 3:15PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A cold front is expected to move southeast from the Chukchi Sea
Saturday night into Sunday, northwesterly winds are expected to
increase across the Kotzebue Sound. Gusts on Sunday are expected
to be between 30 and 40 mph. With this, water levels could rise to
as high as 2 ft above the normal high tide line, with the highest
levels in the Kotzebue Sound.

NWSheadline: Slight Water Level Rises Expected Sunday

properties.areaDesc: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Central Arctic Plains; Central Brooks Range; Romanzof Mountains
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 24 at 3:15PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Another Arctic cold front is expected to move southeast from the
Chukchi Sea Saturday night into Sunday. Starting off, most of the
precipitation will be rain and then transition to snow Saturday
night into early Sunday morning. During this transition, there is
a slight chance for sleet and/or freezing drizzle to fall along
the eastern Arctic Coast. 2-4" of snow is possible in the Brooks
Range and a coating to 2" across the Arctic Coast.

NWSheadline: Wintry Mix Possible Across North Slope with Progressing Cold Front Saturday Night into Sunday

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 24 at 11:08AM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
The Washington State Department of Ecology have issued an Air
Quality Alert until 11 AM PDT Monday.

For the Smoke Air Quality Alert, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 22 at 5:20PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of ozone pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the South Coast Air Basin and Coachella Valley. Levels
of ozone pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and air pollution transport.

* WHEN...until 8 PM Monday. The highest ozone levels typically occur
in the afternoon and early-evening hours.

* IMPACTS... Ozone air pollution can cause serious health problems,
including trouble breathing, asthma attacks, and lung damage.
Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with
lung disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, and grilling

To help minimize outdoor ozone air pollution levels:

* Limit the use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment
until evening hours
* Try to delay trips to the gas station and the use of household
chemicals until the evening
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
